_title: Eight bits wide, and it holds a number C16 cannot
_description: The same machine as C16 with the data path widened: two 74LS189s instead of one, two 74HC283s carry-chained, two registers per register. Nothing conceptual changes — the microcode is the same table — and that is worth seeing once, because widening is the part people expect to be hard and it is only more of the same. What changes is what the machine can HOLD. Load LDA 3, ADD 3, OUT and 100, and the output reads 200: a number four bits cannot represent at all. The ADDRESS path stays four bits on purpose — an instruction is four bits of opcode and four of operand, so sixteen cells is the whole memory and a wider counter would address nothing.
